issues.legal_issue: Forests and trees forming part of an estate vested in the State upon the statutory vesting notification despite a prior contract granting a right to cut trees.
material_facts: A contract with the former proprietor granted a right to cut specified teak trees in a forest forming part of a jagir estate.
A notification under the abolition statute vested the estate in the State after the contract was made.
The claimant sought to enforce the forest rights granted by the former proprietor against the State.
issues.conclusion: The forest and trees vested in the State under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4 of the Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950 provide for proprietary rights, including rights in forests and trees, to vest in the State upon notification, subject to the Act’s exceptions. The claimed interest was not shown to fall within the saving provisions of section 5. Mahadeo v. State of Bombay, State of M.P. v. Yakinuddin, and Mulamchand v. State of M.P. were followed.

predicates.claim_to_enforce_prevesting_forest_contr: A claimant seeks to enforce against the State forest rights granted by a former proprietor before vesting.
predicates.forest_and_trees_were_part_of_vested_est: The forest and trees were part of an estate in which the former proprietor held proprietary rights.
predicates.vesting_notification_applied_to_estate: A notification took effect that vested the estate in the State.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks to enforce a pre-vesting forest contract against the State and the forest and trees were part of an estate covered by a vesting notification, the forest and trees vest in the State.

issues.legal_issue: A contract to cut standing trees does not transfer ownership of the timber as goods before the trees are identified and felled where the contract leaves part of each tree standing.
material_facts: The contract entitled the claimant to cut teak trees meeting a stated girth description, so the qualifying trees had to be identified.
The contract required the stumps to remain above the ground, meaning the whole trees were not to be removed.
The trees had not been felled before the estate vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had not become the owner of the trees as goods; property in the timber could pass only when the trees were felled, and the trees had vested in the State before that occurred.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 19 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, property in unascertained goods does not pass until the goods are ascertained. Trees agreed to be severed may be goods, but here the trees had not been ascertained and the contract did not provide for sale of the whole trees. Property in the cut timber could pass at the earliest upon felling. Sections 3 and 4 of the Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950 governed vesting of the forest and trees in the State; the Court also relied on Mahadeo v. State of Bombay, State of M.P. v. Yakinuddin, and Mulamchand v. State of M.P. on vesting.

predicates.claim_to_enforce_tree_cutting_contract_a: A claimant seeks to enforce against the State a contract granting a right to cut trees.
predicates.standing_trees_required_identification_b: The contract describes the trees to be cut by characteristics that must be checked to identify the qualifying trees.
predicates.contract_required_trees_to_be_felled_bef: The contract contemplates that trees are to be felled before the timber is removed.
predicates.estate_vested_before_felling: The estate vested in the State before the contracted trees were felled.

issues.definition: Where a claimant seeks to enforce a tree-cutting contract against the State, the trees must first be identified and felled, and the estate vested before felling, ownership of the timber does not pass before felling.

issues.legal_issue: A purported acceptance that reserves a right inconsistent with a material condition of an offer does not conclude a contract.
material_facts: The State’s letter stated that the claimant’s tree-cutting claim would be considered only if he gave up his claim to recover the sum already paid and paid an additional sum.
The claimant agreed to pay the additional sum but expressly reserved his right to claim a refund of the sum already paid.
The claimant sought specific performance on the basis that the exchange of letters created a new contract.
issues.conclusion: There was no unconditional acceptance and no concluded contract on the basis of the exchange of letters.
issues.legal_principle: An acceptance must be unconditional to conclude a contract; an acceptance that is conditional or qualified does not accept the offer. The Court also considered it doubtful that the State’s letter was an offer, but held that even if it was, the claimant’s reservation prevented unconditional acceptance. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this issue.

predicates.claim_for_specific_performance_based_on_: A claimant seeks specific performance on the basis that correspondence formed a contract.
predicates.proposed_acceptance_reserved_a_right_inc: The responding letter accepts a proposed bargain while reserving a right that conflicts with a condition stated in the offer.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim rests on correspondence and the proposed acceptance reserves a right inconsistent with an offer condition, no concluded contract arises.
